properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 930580 - Medium Affected: AIR - Suspected Responsible Party: ARCTIC ICE CO
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 930580
Incident Time: 2010-02-04 03:04:00
Nearest City: College Park, GA
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: AMMONIA, ANHYDROUS
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: ARCTIC ICE CO
Skytruth Analysis
CALLER REPORTS THAT A POLICE OFFICER HAD STOPPED AT THE GAS STATION NEXT TO THE ARCTIC ICE CO AND SMELLED AMMONIA. HE CALLED THE FD TO HAVE THEM INVESTIGATE. UPON ARRIVAL THEY FOUND THE PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE GOING OFF. THE FACILITY HAS 2-1000 LB VESSELS OF ANHYDROUS AMMONIA. THEY CLOSED THE STREETS AND THE BP STATION NEXT DOOR AND ATLANTA HAZ MAT TEAM CAME IN FOR ASSISTANCE. THERE WAS A FAILURE IN THE POP OFF VALVE AND THEY LOST APPROXIMATELY 1000 LBS OF AMMONIA WAS RELEASED DURING THE INCIDENT. THEY KEPT THE BUSINESS CLOSED UNTIL MORNING AND THEY HAD A CREW COME IN AND REPAIR THE SYSTEM. THERE WERE NO INJURIES.

Report Description/// 10MAY24 48-HOUR PHMSA UPDATE TO NRC REPORT NUMBER 1398534 /// ON THURSDAY MAY 09 WILLIAMS CALLED THE NRC TO REPORT AN INCIDENT ON LINE2443 IN THE NW PIPELINE SYSTEM NEAR MILEPOST 112.5 IN WOLF CREEK, OREGON. THE INCIDENT OCCURRED DURING THE REMOVAL OF COATING ON THE PIPELINE WHILE COMPLETING AN EXPLORATORY DIG BASED ON AN ILI RUN. CAUSE OF THE LEAK IS CURRENTLY UNDER INVESTIGATION AND MORE INFORMATION WILL BE PROVIDED IN THE 30 DAY REPORT INCLUDING ESTIMATED LEAK VOLUME. THE LEAK WAS TEMPORARILY REMEDIATED WITH A PLIDCO LEAK CLAMP. THERE IS A PRESSURE REDUCTION ON THE LINE SINCE THE ONSET OF THE DIG CONSIDERED REPORTABLE DUE TO AN APPROXIMATE COST TO REPAIR OF $200,000. PERMANENT REPAIR BY CUTOUT IS EXPECTED TO BE COMPLETED 15JUN24. ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION OF INCIDENT: NATURAL GAS RELEASED FROM A 10 INCH PIPELINE THAT WAS FOUND DURING EXCAVATION WHEN THEY LOCATED AN ANOMALY.

properties.content:

Location2: QUIK TRIP GAS STATION

Material: FORMIC ACID
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: ATOTECH
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 34.912855, -80.978203 (Approximated from premise)
Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTS AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF FORMIC ACID WAS RELEASED TO THE AIR, THE BACK OF THEIR VAN, AND STRAPS. THE MATERIAL CAME FROM BLUE 1-2 GALLON CONTAINERS. THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE IS UNKNOWN TO CALLER, THEY BELIEVE THE MATERIAL MAY HAVE BEEN IMPROPERLY PACKAGED. THE INCIDENT OCCURRED WHILE THE VEHICLE WAS IN MOTION. CALLER STATES THEY DROVE 8 MINUTES TO THE GAS STATION. THEY THEN CONTACTED THEIR DISPATCHER AT 1613 INFORMING THEM THAT THEY WERE BEING IMPACTED THE MATERIAL RELEASED. THEY HAD ITCHY EYES, RUNNY NOSE, A HEADACHE, AND THEIR THROAT HURT. DURING THIS TIME CALLER STATES THEY WERE TOLD THE MATERIAL THEY WERE CARRYING WAS NOT A HARMFUL CHEMICAL. ONCE THE MATERIAL WAS TAKEN BACK TO THE FACILITY THEY WERE INFORMED BY THEIR DISPATCHER THAT THE MATERIAL WAS IN FACT A HARMFUL CHEMICAL. CALLER STATES THEIR VAN HAD BEEN LOADED WITH 2,200 POUNDS OF FORMIC ACID. THE MATERIAL WAS IN SMALL 1-2 GALLON CONTAINERS. IT WAS SUPPOSED TO GO TO SANTA ANA, CALIFORNIA. CALLER STATES THEY HAVE IMAGES AVAILABLE UPON REQUEST.
